source.title: Adapting Stepsizes by Momentumized Gradients Improves Optimization and Generalization
source.authors: Yi-Zhou Wang; Yue Kang; Can Qin; Huan Wang; Yi Xu; Yu-Lun Zhang; Y. Fu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper text. Its displayed title metadata conflicts with the paper title in the body: the body title is “Rethinking Adam: A Twofold Exponential Moving Average Approach.”
record.tranche_reason: The study reports optimizer comparisons on natural-label image classification and language tasks, including train and test performance, and argues that its optimizer closes the generalization gap between adaptive methods and SGD. This refines the claim's optimizer-related scope; it does not test random-label memorization or the other mapped conditions.
record.gate_note: Rows below cover the optimizer comparisons on natural-data tasks, which bear on V4 and on the broader natural-label generalization claim. The paper's theory and cited findings about flat minima are not separate empirical rows for V7. Figure 4 and Figures 6–7 are described qualitatively; no curve values are reconstructed from them. CIFAR-10 accuracy rows use Table 2, and ImageNet uses Table 3. Language and GAN test metrics do not directly measure training-to-test error gaps, so they are recorded as findings about the claim's subject under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam, AdamW and other existing adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on held-out image and language metrics. These comparisons test V4 using broader hyperparameter tuning. Held-out perplexity and BLEU are relevant to V4; a numerical training-to-test gap is not required.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they argue AdaMomentum maintains fast convergence, improves over adaptive baselines, matches SGDM on vision tasks and performs best on their other benchmarks. Their claimed closure concerns the performance difference between optimizer families, not a demonstrated elimination of the training-to-test gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes AdaMomentum, changing Adam's second-moment estimate to use momentumized gradients and moving epsilon inside the square root. It compares carefully tuned optimizers on natural-data tasks; it does not test random-label memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice and task/architecture conditions change the reported test metric. The paper describes extensive hyperparameter tuning for all compared optimizers; schedules and tuned parameters vary by task.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaMomentum has the best reported mean perplexity, BLEU and GAN FID among the listed methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed optimizer improves benchmark performance over the selected baselines under the reported tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 5 qualitatively depicts a flatter ResNet-34 loss basin for AdaMomentum than Adam along two random directions, using one seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice changes the displayed local loss landscape; this does not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: The GAN experiments compare FID, and several SNGAN baseline values are attributed to another paper.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizers differ in generative sample quality and training stability in these GAN settings.

record.code_released: The code will be made publicly available after the acceptance of the paper for publication.
record.problems: The reported empirical comparisons concern a newly proposed optimizer and use task-specific extensive hyperparameter tuning; they do not evaluate random labels, the interpolation threshold, or training-to-test error gaps as the primary measure. Figure 4 and language-model curves provide qualitative train/test curves without tabulated values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows beyond the tabled image-classification optimizer comparisons were extracted. Train-accuracy curves in Figure 4 and LSTM train/test perplexity curves in Figures 6–7 are figure-only and lack precise numerical values in the text; test perplexity/BLEU/FID findings are summarized under fits_no_version because they do not directly test V1–V8. GAN and language task table metrics were not assigned claim-version rows.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and random-label training, memorization capacity, and random-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.

A comparison restricted to learning-rate and schedule tuning; a controlled limited-versus-broader tuning intervention; switching Adam to SGD; and numerical verification of equal or better final training performance despite worse held-out performance.
Batch-size interventions under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions; using fixed dropout in LSTMs does not test its benefit.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Add existing-optimizer versus SGDM rows for Table 2, especially AdamW: 93.33±0.15%, 95.48±0.10% and 95.52±0.14% for VGGNet-16, ResNet-34 and DenseNet-121. These results bear directly on the decoupled-weight-decay qualification.

Correct the declared exclusion of language metrics: add SGDM, Adam and AdamW test-perplexity rows for each LSTM depth. SGDM: 85.31±0.09, 67.25±0.20, 63.52±0.16; Adam: 84.55±0.10, 67.11±0.20, 64.10±0.25; AdamW: 88.18±0.14, 73.61±0.15, 69.91±0.20. These are V4 results despite not measuring an explicit train–test gap.

Correct the declared exclusion of translation metrics: add SGDM, Adam and AdamW BLEU rows, 28.22±0.21, 30.14±1.39 and 35.62±0.11, respectively. Record the 55-epoch budget, warmup and last-five-checkpoint averaging.

record.verdict_notes: Only supplied text was used. This study is not an original source of V4. Broader tuning alone is not a scope-limiting result; its consequences must be established by performance comparisons. No limited-versus-broader tuning comparison is reported. The numerical image rows are accurate, but their original supports rationale incorrectly rested on the proposed optimizer. Language results were declared left out, but their exclusion from V4 was substantively incorrect; missing entries request that classification repair. Figure 4's extracted text does not permit reliable numerical final-training comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy using the same architectures and recipes are not compared.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.

The study does not compare only learning rates and decay schedules, broader tuning, or switching from Adam to SGD. It does compare tuned optimizers, including Adam and AdamW, with SGD momentum and reports natural-task test metrics.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No direct comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps or other measures.
